design: Generate two or four explicitly requested forms of the same derived root. Not a full Sanskrit paradigm. No source word or correction trace.
grammar: Reuse reviewed yaN -> Ric -> san composition and canonical upasargas. Classical Kartari, explicit Parasmaipada, exclude Curadi, no aorist.
scoring: All requested rows must be correct. Any VP variant per row accepted. Also report per-form accuracy, JSON validity, refusals, truncation, and completed-answer accuracy.
interpretation: This changes task granularity and strict success probability. It is not evidence of lower single-form accuracy and not directly comparable to the original one-form metric.
source_support: Section 2.3 reports both individual-cell and full-paradigm correctness. Our partial-paradigm design is an adaptation, not the same benchmark.
selection: 160 fresh development tasks, 160 distinct exact citation+gana families; all 480 component forms were unsubmitted. No labels used for task membership.
compute: Initial pilot uses the same xhigh/16384 ceiling as earlier creation pilots. Truncations are separately reported; high-cap validation required before final claims.
sample_size: A paradigm is one scored task. 480 requested forms do not count as 480 independent benchmark items.
